subject: GuideWire - service degradation: latency/errors impacting throughput
messages:
From: Evan Morris <evan.morris@guidewire.com>

Cc: GuideWire SRE <sre@guidewire.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Service report - sudden latency + errors on inference 

Hi Grace / Ben —

We're seeing an urgent production impact starting ~08:45 PST: end-user latency (p50 -> p99) is up ~4x and overall throughput for our tenant dropped ~38%. Error rate spiked to ~12% (500s and 503s tied to model inference calls). We pulled a short diagnostic and saw repeated KV eviction activity and a large queue backlog on the hot lane; traces show many requests waiting behind a small set of blocked batch lanes (head-of-line behavior).

Attached: guidewire_error_snapshot.log (last 60m, traces + token-level latencies).

This is hitting a live feature in three critical regions for us; our SLA window is currently at risk. Can you confirm you're aware and whether Redwood has an immediate mitigation we can apply (we need either a hotfix or a recommended rollback).

We can be on a call: +1 (415) 555-0193.

—Evan

- Increase KV eviction threshold / pin hot prefixes for duration of incident.

Relevant links: HubSpot record attached and our HotLane Mitigation Runbook (see link below). I'm spinning up a Zoom and will send invite.

Date: 2026-11-13T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Service report - sudden latency + errors on inference

Quick triage findings from the cluster (initial):
- Timeline: a config rollback was applied at 07:50 that reverted an experiment which had increased per-tenant cache TTLs and also changed batching scheduling. The rollback restored the prior TTLs but left batching scheduler defaults lowered.
- Symptom: the combination reduced effective cache residency for hot prefixes and concentrated requests into fewer batch lanes. That caused repeated prefix eviction and head-of-line blocking on a few lanes (small number of large batches holding the lane).
- Evidence: eviction spike correlated with a surge of 2-3 keys (hot prefixes) in the attached logs. Latency traces indicate requests queued behind long-running batch assembly.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:40):
1) Increased eviction threshold for GuideWire KV partition (temporary +15%).
2) Disabled continuous batching for tenant (fall back to direct serving) — this reduced queueing but increased per-token CPU; throughput started recovering.
3) Pinned 4 known hot prefixes to the in-memory tier to avoid eviction.

Next steps (recommendations):
- Short-term (next 2 hours): keep continuous batching disabled for GuideWire, monitor throughput and error rate. If stable, reintroduce with smaller max_batch_size and a fast-fail threshold.
- Medium-term (24-72h): promote a patch that tightens batch lane isolation, increases shard slots for high-traffic tenants, and adjusts TTLs for prefix-heavy workloads. I've attached kv-config-diff.patch for the proposed change.

I'll keep updating the thread — Marcus and I are watching dashboards and traces now.

Jonas Weber
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-14T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: Executive summary: GuideWire throughput/error incident (root cause & remediation)

Team / Evan —

Thanks for patience while we stabilized GuideWire's traffic. High-level summary:
- Root cause: an incomplete rollback of a prior experiment changed batching defaults and reduced effective KV residency for a small set of hot prefixes. That combo produced eviction thrash + head-of-line blocking on batch lanes, which increased latency and error rate.
- Immediate mitigation: disabled continuous batching for the tenant, increased eviction thresholds, and pinned hot prefixes. These actions restored throughput to ~95% of baseline and dropped error rate to <1% within ~45 minutes of triage.
- Proposed permanent fixes:
  1) Patch (attached: kv-config-diff.patch) to restore correct TTLs and increase shard slots for tenant isolation.
  2) Change rollout policy: require a canary with hot-prefix synthetic traffic for batching/cache config changes.
  3) Alerting: add a pair of synthetic checks (hot prefix eviction rate + batch lane queue length) to detect this class of failure earlier.

Requested approvals:
- Approve config patch promotion to prod (short maintenance window, immediate rollback capability).
- Approve issuing a service credit if HubSpot confirms SLA breach for the affected window.

Attachments: hotlane-mitigation-playbook.pdf, kv-config-diff.patch.

I'll schedule a 1-hour post-mortem tomorrow to finalize follow-ups and owners.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
